To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deletions of a region on chromosome 9, encompassing four Mendelian disease-causing genes, are responsible for multisystems disorders including intellectual disability and epilepsy.
9q deletion encompassing combinations of STXBP1 and ENG, STXBP and SPTAN, and TOR1 and STXBP1 are responsible for progressive encephalopathies, vascular dysplasia and dystonia.
deletions in 9q34 encompassing four Mendelian disease-causing genes, STXBP, SPTAN, ENG, and TO1R, result in a spectrum of complex clinical phenotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular basis of a number of rare genetic disorders.
the study of the 9q 34.11 region in the context of deletions, which are associated with intellectual disability and epilepsy.
the identification of the genetic causes of intellectual disability and epilepsy, and the delineation of the phenotypic spectrum of the disorders caused by the identified genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
9q 34.11 genomic deletion involving STXBP1 gene is responsible for progressive encephalopathic disorder characterized by intellectual disability, epilepsy, movement disorder, and autism.

the 9q deletions encompassing the four dosage-sensitive genes STXBP1 (epilepsy, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder), TOR1A (early-onset primary dystonias, intellectual disability), ENG (hereditary hemorrhagic telangectasia), and SPTAN 1 (infantile epileptic enphalopathy, infant spasms, hypomyelination, and intellectual disability) result in multisystemic phenotypes.

the 9q 34.11 deletional syndromes are a result of the haploinsufficiencies of the four genes: STXBPI, SPTAN, ENG and TOR1A and that these deletions may be associated with the clinical features of the four genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

9q deletions involving STXBP1 may result in intellectual disability and epilepsy, and deletions involving TOR1A, ENG, and SPTAM1 may result in dystonia, HHT and/or intellectual disability, respectively.
deletions of 9q34 are a common cause of developmental delay and/or intellectual disability, and may be associated with a number of additional features.
deletions in the 9 q34 region are associated with a wide variety of symptoms and syndromes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical features of patients with 9 Mb 9q34 deletions may be explained by the deletion of a few genes in the region.
the clinical phenotype of a 9q34 gene deletion is dependent on the specific genes that are deleted.
the 9q deletion phenotype is highly variable, and the presence of a specific gene in the deletion does not necessarily predict the clinical phenotype.
